programmes.d: At Bridlington's Spa Royal Hall, the team nominate their ideal age of elegance.
Fiona Bruce and the team of experts are in Dundee.
The show is recorded in the former drawing offices of Harland and Wolff where the Titanic was conceived.
Items discovered include a photograph of Winston Churchill and an old theatrical costume.
Medicine chest from early Victorian times, complete with many intact medicines; a historic document marking the end of World War II; a pair of rare Irish plate buckets.
Objects found in Dulwich include an early illustration by madcap artist Heath Robinson.
Items in Bishop's Palace in Wells, Somerset, include a painting, and a plate possibly found in Captain Scott's tent on the ill-fated Antarctic expedition.
Fiona Bruce and the team return to the Spa Royal Hall in Bridlington.
Objects include a bracelet once gifted by Queen Victoria; small seal used by campaigners for the abolition of slavery; tapestry.
Fiona Bruce and the team brave the wet weather at Oxburgh Hall in Norfolk.
Miniature clock smuggled out of Germany in World War II; world's first copying machine; letter sent to a conscientious objector.
Fiona Bruce and the team choose their favourite moments and give updates on star items.
Photograph of Winston Churchill; theatrical costume from the early days of pantomime; valuable painting.
The team is in Samares Manor in Jersey, objects from all over the world are examined.
An early illustration by madcap artist Heath Robinson; a set of rare miniatures; a book returned after a 50-year loan.
Fiona Bruce takes the team to the Lancashire coast for a day in the Blackpool Tower Ballroom.
Artifacts of HMS Falcon excavated from the sea bed; rare buttons commemorating the Battle of Quebec in 1759; an account of life as a Japanese prisoner of war.
Fiona Bruce and the team return for a second visit to the Tower Ballroom in Blackpool.
A Cartier diamond and ruby ring; RAF Pathfinder items; Moorcroft pottery.
Fiona Bruce and the team return with a second helping from a recent visit to Hertford College.
The team head for Devon's beautiful Tamar Valley, and weigh anchor at Morwellham Quay.
A one pound boot sale buy went on to become the best investment in the show's history.
Members of the public at Lincoln Cathedral have their antiques valued by experts.
At Samares Manor in Jersey, objects from all over the world are examined.
A second visit to Lincoln Cathedral, members of the public have their antiques valued by experts.
A bible containing handwritten extracts from Charlotte Brontë; images drawn under fire by a war artist; boot sale brooch.
Fiona Bruce and the team are in County Durham for a visit to The Bowes Museum.
Prayer book; valuable pair of dueling pistols; the original Teddy from "Watch with Mother."
Experts welcome thousands to Bletchley Park, home of the Enigma code-breaking team in World War Two.
Objects at Hertford College in Oxford include a Beatles recording session, a Maori carving and a Russian painting.
A return visit to Bletchley Park near Milton Keynes for Fiona Bruce and the experts.
Brown jug; silver salver; a long case clock.
Fiona Bruce and the team visit Burghley House near Stamford in Lincolnshire.
Searching for hidden treasures and antiques in Lincoln, England.
The experts head to the Scottish borders at Abbotsford, once the home of Sir Walter Scott.
Chinese picture bought for a song; a Georgian dining table; a collection of early TV implements first used to screen the Queen's Coronation.
The team sets sail for the Channel Islands where the people of Guernsey give them a warm welcome.
A silver box given in thanks when troops liberated the Netherlands in World War Two; chairs.
Fiona Bruce and the team arrive at Brooklands Motor Racing and Aviation Museum.
Items up for auction in Bletchley Park include a pair of important candlesticks, as well as pieces rescued from the golden age of British liners.
At the Brooklands Museum, the objects of note include books once owned by Churchill.
Items up for auction in Bletchley Park include an ornate vase rescued at the last minute from the dishwasher and a teddy bear with a surprising story.
Fiona Bruce and the experts arrive at Aberglasney Gardens, where they find a deluge of treasures.
Searching for hidden treasures and antiques at the Burghley House of Stamford, England.
Fiona Bruce and the team are in Bath where thousands flock to with their treasured objects.
A bottle used by smugglers to fool customs men; a miniature battle scene hand cut by a prisoner during World War I; dinner service fit for a queen.
A second helping from Bath, where visitors are welcomed to the magnificent Assembly Rooms.
A piece of furniture used as target practice by the Germans; a giant sapphire once owned by a Maharajah; a single banknote worth a fortune.
